title: 2nd Congressional District in Illinois election candidates Donna Miller, Mike Noack, Ashley Banks make cases to voters - ABC7 Chicago
text:
2nd Congressional District in Illinois election candidates Donna Miller, Mike Noack, Ashley Banks make cases to voters - ABC7 Chicago

 Illinois' 2nd Congressional District candidates make cases to voters ahead of Election Day 
 Candidates running to represent Illinois' 2nd Congressional District are making their cases to voters ahead of Election Day. WLS By Leah Hope Wednesday, October 21, 2026 12:50AM Share KANKAKEE, Ill. (WLS) -- Illinois' 2nd Congressional District is diverse in many ways.
 It runs south from Chicago's South Side through the south suburbs to Kankakee and to Danville. It has been represented by Democrat Robin Kelly since 2012, but she left office for an unsuccessful run for Senate.
 ABC7 Chicago is now streaming 24/7. Click here to watch 
 And the district that hugs the Indiana border going south could be important as Republicans try to hold on to a thin majority in the midterms.
 Democrat Donna Miller won the primary, beating candidates including Jesse Jackson Jr., who previously represented the district. She is a Cook County commissioner and a former healthcare executive.
 "Experience matters and being able to get things done matter. I think knowing how government works is important," Miller said.
 Miller lives in the south suburbs and shares that her family history goes back to a small family farm in Champaign County.
 "We have a competitive farm industry here in Illinois, and they should be competing not only here within the United States, but even on a global level," Miller said.
 Republican Mike Noack lives in a small town, west of Kankakee. He is a truck driver and has never run for political office until now.
 "The average citizen we're struggling to survive. We, I just, the government isn't working. OK, back in the day they used to compromise, they used to negotiate, they used to get stuff done. Now, they don't do that," Noack said.

 Noack says he understands the need to simplify the nation's immigration system, as his wife was born in Japan, and that is among the issues with which he disagrees with the current administration.
 "I do agree with a lot of stuff they are doing, but there are things that I don't agree with, also," Noack said.
 Ashley Banks is an independent running as a write-in candidate. She's from Chicago but says she moved to Kankakee to hear more for downstate residents.
 "I've spoke with the people, the voters, and they have told me that they don't feel as if they're being heard in the rural area of Illinois," Banks said.
 Banks is a former CTA bus driver and freelance journalist who had a rare childhood condition that required several surgeries. She has never run for political office before.
 "I do understand that it is a risk, but at the same time, if we have leaders who have not done the job, then I am willing to step up," Banks said.
 It will be up to voters of the 2nd Congressional District who represents them in Washington. Early voting is underway, and Election Day is Nov. 3.
